items.title: constexpr algorithms
items.body:
add constexpr support to the following core facilities:
- distance / enumerate
- range / sized_range / make_range / range::get
- range_iterface
  add constexpr support to the following facilities in utility/functional:
- as function
- with_braced_init_args
- operators
- reference_wrapper
- ref_fn / ref
- add greater as a synonym for operator> (requires WeaklyOrdered and EqualityComparable)
  add c++14 constexpr support to utility/move
  add c++14 constexpr support to safe_int and add constexpr swap function to safe_int
  bugfix: set_difference test

The following algorithms can be used within constexpr functions with minimal to no changes to the 
algorithm implementation: 
- adjacent_find
- all_of
- any_of
- binary_search
- copy
- copy_backward
- copy_if
- copy_n
- count
- count_if
- equal
- equal_range
- fill
- fill_n
- find
- find_end
- find_first_of
- find_if
- find_if_not
- for_each
- generate
- generate_n
- includes
- inplace_merge (unbuffered)
- is_heap
- is_heap_until
- is_partitioned
- is_sorted
- is_sorted_until
- lexicographical_compare
- lower_bound
- make_heap
- max_element
- merge
- merge_move
- min_element
- minmax_element
- mismatch
- move
- move_backward
- none_of
- partition
- partition_copy
- partition_move
- partition_point
- push_heap
- random_shuffle (for user-provided constexpr random number generators)
- remove
- remove_copy
- remove_copy_if
- remove_if
- replace
- replace_copy
- replace_copy_if
- replace_if
- reverse_copy
- rotate
- rotate_copy
- search
- search_n
- set_difference
- set_intersection
- set_symmetric_difference
- set_union
- shuffle\* (for user-provided constexpr uniform random number generators)
- sort_heap
- stable_partition
- stable_sort
- swap_ranges
- transform
- unique
- unique_copy
- upper_bound

[*] shuffle: requires a constexpr uniform_int_distribution that has been adapted from 
libc++ (with minimal changes), but no real changes to the algorithm itself. For testing purposes, the linear_congruential_engine from libc++ has been adapted (with minimal changes).

The following algorithms haven’t been adapted yet because goto is not allowed within constexpr functions and as a consequence the algorithms would have to be rewritten: 
- nth_element
- is_permutation

This is doable, and I partially did so for stable_partition, but I would like to know what you think.

The following algorithms are constexpr but use iter_swap. Since iter_swap requires indirect_swap and thus swap to be constexpr, they won’t be constexpr for most types (e.g. int, they work for `safe_int<int>` because it has a constexpr swap): 
- sort_heap
- pop_heap
- inplace_merge
- next_permutation
- partial_sort
- partial_sort_copy
- partition
- prev_permutation
- random_shuffle
- reverse
- shuffle
- stable_partition
- swap_ranges

I’ve tested these with safe_int by adding a friend swap function to safe_int. It might be better to add this functions for testing only, and not in general to safe int, since it overrides the default swap for the underlying type and does not perform ADL. 

On the usage of temporary buffers (note this discussion is now taking place in [this issue](https://github.com/ericniebler/range-v3/issues/168)):

I think it is :
- wrong for algorithms to allocate memory by default,
- even wronger that users cannot opt out of this behavior,
- bad that users cannot pass these algorithms preallocated buffers.

In libstdc++ and libc++ get_temporary_buffer just calls new in a loop. 
So even tho I can understand the good intentions behind get_temporary_buffer, I think that the way this is handled by the STL right now is far from optimal. 

The algorithms that use it directly are:
- stable_partition
- inplace_merge

And the algorithms that use these algorithms are:
- stable_sort

I’ve provided these algorithms with a constexpr member function called `inplace` that uses no buffer.
It will be better to provide them with another member function called `with_buffer` that allows the user to specify a buffer (such a stack allocated buffer). 

I'd rather leave this as is (with inplace) and open an issue where we can discuss this on its own, since I think is one of the things that is worth to get right on an STL2 (and maybe try to unify get_temporary_buffer with Allocator).

items.title: Constexpr support
items.body:
Adds C++14 constexpr support
- adds macros to detect the language version: 
  - `RANGES_CXX_GREATER_THAN_11` for C++>11 (e.g. C++14/17/...)
  - `RANGES_CXX_GREATER_THAN_14` for C++>14 (e.g. C++17/...)
- adds macro to enable relaxed constexpr support in C++>11:
  - `RANGES_RELAXED_CONSTEXPR` 
  - note in C++11 the macro is defined to `inline`
- add CMake option to choose with which language std the tests should be compiled:
  - `-DRANGES_CXX_STD=value` => `-std=c++value`,  `value={11,14,17,1y,1z}` (defaults to `11`).
- set up travis to test in both C++11 and C++14
- set up travis to test with:
  - gcc-4.9 (libstdc++)
  - clang-3.4, clang-3.5, clang-3.6, clang-3.7 (libc++)
- set up valgrind with CMake and travis 
  - note: all tests are run both with and without valgrind in all configurations
- add utilities: 
  - constexpr friendly array (used for testing)
  - constexpr reverse_iterator (used for rbegin/rend/...)

**Lessons learned**
- [x] `constexpr` functions are instantiated in unevaluated contexts (yes, really!)
  - Solution: don't use `-> decltype(...)` for SFINAE. Seriously, just don't, use `enable_if` or similar instead. 
  - Otherwise... different branches will be taken at compile time in C++14 is some of the functions involved are marked `constexpr`. This is particularly bad for customization points since some users might mark theirs `constexpr` and others won't. The alternatives are more verbose but work fine and are in general more explicit (concepts, enable_if, ...). 
  - In a nutshell: your code shall not break when removing the trailing return types (`-> decltype(...)`) in C++14.

**Currently work-in-progress ("// TODO: [constexpr]")**:
- [ ] Set up travis to test range-v3 under MacOS using AppleClang + libc++.
- [ ] -Wundefined-inline: `constexpr` implies `inline` which introduces some visibility warnings.
- [x] Rethink general workarounds:
  - [x] `std::bind` is not `constexpr` (a one parameter parameter "binder" `binder_` is implemented in functional)
  - [x] `constexpr` functions are instantiated in unevaluated contexts (out of luck here)
- [x] Open issues (haven't given them enough thought):
  - [x] Should only non-mutable algorithms/views be implemented? 
    - No, mutable algorithms/views can also be made constexpr and used in a "non-constexpr"y way inside `constexpr` functions.
    - Old note: mutating `begin` and `end` member functions cannot mutate the algorithm state if this is `constexpr`. Update: but this is not `constexpr` if not marked as such inside a `constexpr` function. 
  - [x] Should actions be implemented?
    - Yes, same rationale as for mutable algorithms/views.
- [ ] Clean-up: fix all todos, rebase, remove all whitespace changes, ...
  - [ ] remove advance_to_fn from range_fwd (is superseded by advance)
  - [ ] check license in new files
  - [ ] check for uses of `std::ref` instead of `ranges::ref`

Make most of range-v3 constexpr:
- [ ] core:
  - [x] `begin`/`end`/`rbegin`/`rend`...
  - [x] `at`/`size`/`empty`/`front`/`back`
  - [x] `move` + `indirect_move`
  - [x] `swap` (doesn't add std::swap to ADL anymore because it is not constexpr)
  - [ ] `distance`
    - rethink distance as customization point
  - [ ] note: add issue `data` non-member function 
  - [ ] `range_adaptor`: discuss with eric the mutable member:  `/*mutable*/ base_range_t rng_;` 
- [x] utility:
  - [x] `variant` impl is not constexpr and works (at least for the tests)
    - Note: feels like duck-tape, I think it is better to reconsider the design of `tagged_variant` from scratch. For example Eggs.Variant is a 1:1 constexpr-compliant replacement to `tagged_variant`, with:
      
      ``` c++
         template<typename... Ts>
         using tagged_variant = eggs::variant<Ts...>;
         using eggs::variants::get;
         template<std::size_t I, typename...Ts, typename U>
         RANGES_RELAXED_CONSTEXPR
         void set(tagged_variant<Ts...> &var, U &&u)
         {
             var = std::forward<U>(u);
         }
         /// + replace all calls to is_valid() with nothing (it has an explicit operator bool that does that)
      ```
      
      I've added an `explicit operator bool() -> is_valid()` to ease the transition if desired, but it is currently not used.
    - note: if all types are trivially destructible, then the destructor is defaulted and variant is constexpr
  - [x] `optional` depends on `variant`
  - [x] `semiregular` depends on `variant` and `optional`
  - [x] `common_tuple` / `common_pair`
    - Note these should be reconsidered with `constexpr` in mind
- [ ] algorithms:
  - [x] `all_of`/`any_of`/`none_of`
  - [x] `adjacent_find`
  - [x] `binary_search`
  - [x] `copy` / `copy_if` / `copy_n` / `copy_backward`
  - [x] `count`/`count_if`
  - [x] `equal` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `fill`/`fill_n`
  - [x] `find`/`find_if`/ `find_if_not`
  - [x] `find_end`

  - [x] `heap_algorithm`(`is_heap_until`/`is_heap`/`push_heap` / `pop_heap` / `make_heap`/`sort_heap`)
  - [x] `inplace_merge` (unbuffered)
    - [ ] Add issue about exposing the non-allocating `inplace_merge` unbuffered in the API
  - [x] `is_partitioned`

  - [ ] `stable_sort`
  - [ ] `swap_ranges`
  - [ ] `transform`

- [ ] views:
  - [ ] `all`: 
  - [x] `iota` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `generate`/`generate_n` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `join` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `repeat`/`repeat_n` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `take` (implementation + tests)
  - [x] `take_exactly`
  - [x] `transform` (implementation + tests)
    - [ ] note: issue #131 is not fixed yet
  - [x] `filter`/ `remove_if`:
    - Old note: amortized mutating `begin` and `end` cannot mutate the range if it is ~~~a constant expression (i.e. const)~~~ constant, but they can mutate a non-constant range within a constant expression.
  - [x] `reverse` (implementation + tests)
